content: Administer four tablets orally every six hours with liquid. Additionally, administer two tablespoons orally every 12 hours for three to four days, followed by one to two tablespoons at bedtime. This regimen is intended for constipation but is not recommended for children. For children, one to two tablespoons can be mixed with milk or cereal and given orally once daily or every 12 hours for three to four days, followed by one to two tablespoons at bedtime, with eight ounces of fluid accompanying each dose. For single feedings, administer one to two teaspoons. Malt soup extract and deflazacort both reduce serum potassium levels. Use these with caution and monitor the patient closely. Malt soup extract also decreases the effects of sodium picosulfate through an unspecified interaction mechanism. The clinical significance of this interaction is minor or unknown, but close monitoring is advised. Potential adverse effects include flatulence, fecal impaction, excessive bowel activity, hypersensitivity reactions, nausea, vomiting, bowel obstruction, appendicitis, dysphagia, rectal bleeding, and gastrointestinal (GI) perforation. Before administration, rule out GI obstruction or perforation. Exercise caution in patients with severe active ulcerative colitis. Regarding pregnancy, this medication is classified as Category B, meaning it is generally considered safe as controlled studies in pregnant women have shown no evidence of fetal risk. For lactation, there is no available data, but since the medication is not absorbed systemically, it is unlikely to pose a risk to breastfeeding infants.
